summary:
Read-only audit of src/features/training (~17.9k lines) plus its Daily, Home and AI consumers. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` is clean, so everything below is a logic, data-path or duplication problem, not a type error.

How it is built today: TrainingPage.tsx is one route with 4 pill tabs (Hevy / Strava / Health / Coach) and a right rail. The rail shows TrainingCalendar, or HealthStatsPanel when the Health tab is open, with NextSessionBanner underneath. The Hevy tab has 7 more sub-tabs. Reads mostly go through hooks with qk keys and STALE times. There is no bare useMutation, and no component calls supabase directly (api files do: ptCoachApi and coachContext query tables inline).

The real problems are these:
(1) The same concept is computed several times with different rules and different data. Examples: bodyweight (5+ readers, none of them uses body_composition_reports), sessions per week (4 definitions), next training session (3), muscle volume (3), per-exercise verdicts (progress-engine vs TrainingInsightsPanel), estimated 1RM (2 formulas), PRs (2 sources), AI coach context (2 builders), sleep merge (client + ai-proxy + phone-gateway).
(2) The same action goes to the database by different routes. Edit routine goes through hevy-api, but Delete routine only deletes the local copy and the next sync brings it back. Log workout sends a payload that breaks the Hevy schema rules the routine builder documents. Manual sleep writes to health_metrics straight from the browser.
(3) Real bugs:
- The Strava OAuth callback is never handled.
- PRs are built from at most 1000 unordered sets.
- Health stats show "—" on today's Day view.
- Free-text limitations show a blank name in the list and "undefined" in the coach snapshot.
- Saving a body measurement does not refresh the Progress bodyweight data.
- Workout cards never show their exercise count or muscle chips.
- The workout detail shows every set as weight × reps, so timed and distance exercises read "— × —".
- Every past planned session in the calendar is red ("missed"), even on days a workout was logged.
- "Latest" mini metrics such as VO2 max usually show "—".
- Days are split in UTC in some places and local time in others.
(4) Dead code and dead features: the per-exercise half of progressDecisions and progressCopy, two unused hevyApi fetchers, useHealthMetrics, the unused 'training' invalidation group, muscle preferences that nothing reads, target overrides with no editor, and training_age_years.
(5) Ten components are over 250 lines. WorkedMuscles (807) and TrainingCalendar (679) are the worst; hevyApi.ts alone is 702 lines.

What splitting out Health involves: move healthApi, useHealthExport, healthAggregate, healthMetrics, recoveryAggregate (shared with Training), bodyCompositionApi and its aggregate/hook, components/health/** and HealthTab into src/features/health. Then add a /health route and a nav entry, and move BarLineChart, axisFormat and chartKit into shared/ui/charts because Training charts use them too. Training, Daily, AI coach and the verify scripts import these today; the full list is in healthCouplings.

Missing data for the requested health context: no age, sex or height is stored anywhere (athlete_profile has goal, experience, training days, equipment and notes only). VO2 max, resting heart rate, body fat and step norms depend on age and sex, so these fields must be added before the Health page can say how good or bad a number is.

Training "clarity" gaps:
- The current program (the owner's "plan") is buried in the Coach → Profile modal.
- There is no "next session: exercise × sets × target load" view. It is only available by expanding each row of the decision table.
- Completed planned sessions are deleted rather than marked done, so planned-vs-done adherence cannot be computed.
- The AI coach never sees the deterministic engine's decisions, so it can contradict the Progress tab.

findings.title: Strava OAuth callback is never handled (redirect lands on /training, parser lives only in Developer → Connections)
findings.evidence: stravaApi.ts:5 `const REDIRECT_URI = `${window.location.origin}${window.location.pathname}#/training``. The only code that reads `?code=` is StravaWidget's useEffect, and StravaWidget is mounted only in ConnectionsTab (grep: no other mount). After consenting, the user lands on #/training?code=… where nothing exchanges the code, so the connection never completes.
findings.fix: Point REDIRECT_URI at `#/developer?tab=connections`, or move the code-exchange effect out of StravaWidget into useAppBootstrap/a tiny `useStravaOAuthCallback()` that runs on every shell route. Then StravaWidget only renders status.

findings.title: Personal Records are computed from at most 1000 arbitrary sets (no pagination, no order, normal sets only)
findings.evidence: fetchHevyPRs: `supabase.from('hevy_sets').select('exercise_template_id, weight_kg, reps, hevy_exercise_id').eq('type', 'normal').not('weight_kg','is',null)`, with no .range loop and no .order. The repo's own healthApi.ts:72-75 records that PostgREST caps every response at 1000 rows. Followed by `.in('id', exerciseIds)` over every exercise id seen. 'failure' sets (often the heaviest) are excluded, and ties keep the first set seen instead of the one with more reps.
findings.fix: Add an SQL view/RPC `hevy_exercise_bests` (per template: max weight with its reps and workout date, times_performed, best e1RM), or page through sets ordered by id. Include failure/dropset per a documented rule and break ties by reps. Use the same source for the engine's PR events (see T11).

findings.title: Log workout sends a payload that breaks the Hevy schema rules the routine path documents; end_time = start_time; weight × reps only
findings.evidence: The payload includes exercise `index`, `title`, `supersets_id` and set `index`. routineForm.ts:119-122 says 'any extra key triggers a "… is not allowed" 400. Notably: no exercise index/title, no set index/rpe, superset_id is singular'. handleCreateWorkout forwards the payload untouched. `end_time: start, // Hevy requires end_time` makes every web-logged workout 0 minutes long (breaks Home minutes, calendar durations). Sets only have weight/reps inputs, so duration/distance exercises cannot be logged.
findings.fix: Extract a shared `toHevyExercisePayload(exercise, templateType)` next to formToPayload (superset_id, no index/title; set fields from setFieldsForType) and reuse RoutineFormParts' SetRow in the log modal. Add a duration/end-time input. Verify with one live create_workout call, per the repo's no-speculative-schema rule.

findings.title: 'Delete routine' only deletes the local mirror, so the next Sync brings it back (create/edit go through Hevy)
findings.evidence: `deleteHevyRoutineLocal` runs `supabase.from('hevy_routines').delete().eq('id', id)`. The confirm text says 'removes it from your local data'. hevy-incremental-sync refreshRoutines upserts every routine Hevy returns (`supabase.from('hevy_routines').upsert(...)`) and only deletes local rows Hevy no longer has, so the routine reappears on the next Sync. current_program_routines and training tasks keep pointing at the deleted id.
findings.fix: Replace it with an explicit 'Hide from this app' (a local hidden flag or table the sync never touches), or remove the button and explain that routines are deleted in the Hevy app. Never delete the mirror row directly.

findings.title: Free-text limitation patterns render a blank name in the list and 'undefined' in the PT coach snapshot
findings.evidence: LimitationsList: `{MOVEMENT_PATTERN_LABEL[item.movement_pattern]}`. ptCoachApi: `Kısıtlama: ${MOVEMENT_PATTERN_LABEL[lim.movement_pattern]} (${lim.severity})`. movement_pattern is free text in the DB and ai-proxy writes it (CLAUDE.md records live rows 'heavy_hip_hinge' and 'unilateral_balance_left', which match none of the 9 enum keys), so the label resolves to undefined.
findings.fix: Add `movementPatternLabel(p) = MOVEMENT_PATTERN_LABEL[p] ?? humanize(p)` and use it everywhere (list, coach snapshot, insights). Normalise at write time: the AI catalog rule should list the 9 keys, and the list should offer 'map to…' for unknown patterns so PATTERN_AFFECTED_SLUGS applies.

findings.title: Health stats rail shows '—' for every number on the Day view of today
findings.evidence: `function completed(series){ const t = todayStr(); return series.filter(d => d.date !== t) }` is applied through split() and directly in OverviewStats. For period='day' with anchor = today the window is [today, today], so every current[] is empty and every stat renders '—' with 'Days with data 0'.
findings.fix: Only drop the in-progress day when averaging a multi-day window. In Day mode show today's partial value labelled 'so far today'. Cover it with a small sucrase verify script.

findings.title: Saving a body measurement doesn't refresh Progress bodyweight, relative strength or insights
findings.evidence: useUpsertBodyMeasurement has `invalidates: [qk.hevy.measurementsAll]` = ['hevy','measurements']. useBodyweightHistory is keyed `qk.hevy.bodyweightHistory(fromStr,toStr)` = ['hevy','bodyweight-history',…] with STALE.long, so the prefix never matches and the Progress 'Bodyweight' card stays stale for up to 10 minutes after a weigh-in.
findings.fix: Add `bodyweightHistoryAll: ['hevy','bodyweight-history']` (or a `bodyweight` invalidation group covering hevy measurements, health weight and body composition) and invalidate it from the upsert, the manual-sleep-style writers and the Hevy syncs.

findings.title: Five or more different bodyweight resolvers, and none of them reads the smart scale actually in use (body_composition_reports)
findings.evidence: fetchBodyweightHistory merges hevy_body_measurements with health_metrics.weight_body_mass. useNutritionCoach takes a 7-point mean of health_metrics only. ptCoachApi, coachContext and HealthCard read health_metrics only, over 30-day windows. BodySection.tsx:98-100 states the Smart Scale Reports panel covers 'the scale actually in use', yet no consumer reads body_composition_reports. The same person gets different kg (or a stale kg) on Progress, Food protein targets, the AI coach and the Daily card.
findings.fix: Create one `bodyweightApi.fetchBodyweightSeries(from,to)` plus `useBodyweightSeries` in the health feature. Merge sources with explicit priority (manual Hevy > smart scale > Apple Health), tag every point with its source, and use it in all seven places. Keep the raw per-source panels for display.

findings.title: Two per-exercise verdict engines on the Progress page can contradict each other
findings.evidence: The top of the page (progress-engine) evaluates current-program sets with the least-squares (linearFit) trend. TrainingInsightsPanel (same page, supporting section) runs `computeExerciseTrendFindings` over ALL 182-day history with `v0 = mean(first 3) … v1 = mean(last 3)` and gates on `repRangeVariedSignificantly(points)`. CLAUDE.md says the engine retired that check because it flags monotonic climbs as 'high variation'. One exercise can read 'Possible plateau' in the table and 'is progressing' in Training Analysis.
findings.fix: Delete rule F in trainingInsights and feed the insights panel the engine's ExerciseProgressResult (trend and currentAction), or render the engine's own labels. Keep the whole-program rules (consistency, volume, rep range) where they are.

findings.title: Two different exercise-progress charts for the same exercise (different data scope, metric and chart tech)
findings.evidence: DecisionDetail's ExerciseChart draws hand-rolled div bars from `buildRepresentativePoints` (representative weight, current-program sets only), spaced by index with no time axis. ExerciseProgressChart (recharts BarLineChart) plots `computeExerciseProgression` (best-set est1RM or volume over all history). Opening the same lift in both shows different numbers.
findings.fix: Keep one ExerciseTrendChart (recharts, real date axis, load-change markers) fed by engine points, with an optional 'all history' toggle. Use it in the drill-down and delete ExerciseProgressChart plus the div-bar chart.

findings.title: 'PR' events claim all history but see only 182 days of current-program sets, while the PR tab uses all-time (capped) max weight
findings.evidence: events.ts header: 'deterministic, all-history achievement detection. Never windowed'. The engine's input is useTrainingHistory (`WINDOW_DAYS = 182`), further narrowed by filterToCurrentProgram. A LOAD_PR chip can fire for a weight below a best from 7 months ago or from an older routine, and the Personal Records tab (normal sets only, truncated) disagrees.
findings.fix: Pass a per-exercise all-time best (from the T02 view) into evaluateExerciseProgress for PR events, or relabel the chips 'best in 6 months'. Use one PR definition across the PR tab, Top 5 and the engine.

findings.title: Two estimated-1RM formulas; the comment claims they match exactly
findings.evidence: HevyPRList declares its own `function est1RM(weightKg, reps){ if (reps == null || reps <= 0) return null; … weightKg * (1 + reps / 30) }` with no rep cap. progressAggregate: `const EST_1RM_MAX_REPS = 12 … if (reps <= 0 || reps > EST_1RM_MAX_REPS) return null`, with the comment 'Matches the existing Personal Records feature's formula EXACTLY'. A 15-rep PR shows an e1RM in the PR peek that the Progress charts refuse to compute.
findings.fix: Delete the local copy and import progressAggregate.est1RM. Show 'n/a above 12 reps' in the peek.

findings.title: Calendar marks every past planned session red ('missed') even when that day was trained, and completed plans are deleted (no adherence history)
findings.evidence: `function planTone(dateStr, todayStr){ if (dateStr === todayStr) return 'warn'; return dateStr > todayStr ? 'info' : 'danger' }` looks at the date only, never at whether a workout exists that day. Projected recurring occurrences therefore show red next to a green workout every past Mon/Wed/Fri. A matched plan is removed entirely: the server deletes the task (the block cascades), and 'Close out' calls `deleteTask.mutate(matchedTask)`. Planned-vs-done can never be reported.
findings.fix: Reconcile per day: give a plan the success tone when a workout with the same routine_id or on the same day exists. Mark the training task done (status='done') instead of deleting it, and keep the block, so adherence ('4 of 5 planned sessions done') becomes computable. That also answers the owner's 'see my plan'.

findings.title: 'Next training session' is derived three ways; two ignore recurring training templates
findings.evidence: useTodayOverview's header says 'the training card should all read this instead of re-deriving it'. It projects recurring templates (`projectRecurringBlocksForDay`). NextSessionBanner uses `useTrainingBlocks(today, to)` only, and TrainingCard uses `useTimeBlocks(date)` filtered to category 'training'. A user with a recurring Mon/Wed/Fri session sees no banner and 'Rest day — nothing planned' on Daily.
findings.fix: Add a shared `useTrainingPlan(from,to)` (one-off plus projected recurring, the same helper TrainingCalendar uses). Base NextSessionBanner, TrainingCard, useTodayOverview and the calendar on it.

findings.title: 'Sessions this week' has four definitions; Progress adherence shows last week's count when nothing is logged yet this week
findings.evidence: The Workouts tab counts Hevy workouts since Monday (local time). Home counts Hevy + Strava since Monday. ProgressOverview uses `consistencyWeeks[consistencyWeeks.length - 1]?.sessionCount`, the LAST LOGGED week (the dense series ends at the latest week with data), labelled 'this week, so far', and only for current-program sets. The PT coach uses a rolling 7 days: `Son 7 günde ${thisWeek.length} antrenman`.
findings.fix: One pure `weekTrainingSummary(workouts, activities, weekStart)` with an explicit definition (Hevy sessions; Strava shown separately). Adherence must look up the current Monday and return 0 when absent. Use it on all four screens.

findings.title: Three muscle-volume computations with different credit rules; WorkedMuscles re-implements muscleMap helpers
findings.evidence: WorkedMuscles credits primary 1.0 and secondary 0.5 over fetchMuscleVolume, builds its own `tplById` (duplicating buildTemplateMuscleMap) and its own `flagsBySlug` (duplicating limitedSlugsFromLimitations). WeeklySetsPerMuscleChart and Insights use computeWeeklySetsPerMuscleTrend over fetchTrainingHistory. The PT coach sums PRIMARY ONLY over 7 days (`'HAFTALIK HACİM (sert set/hafta, birincil kas)'`) after a second templates query, so the AI quotes different set counts from the Muscles tab.
findings.fix: One `computeMuscleDose(sets, templates, {from,to})` in muscleMap/progressAggregate over useTrainingHistory rows, used by Muscles, the charts, Insights and both coach contexts. Delete fetchMuscleVolume/useMuscleVolume and the local maps.

findings.title: Two AI coach context builders (PT Coach tab vs Ask-AI Coach mode) with duplicated summarizers, hard-coded split, and no engine decisions
findings.evidence: summarizeSets (ptCoachApi) and setStr (coachContext) are the same function. Both fetch profile, limitations, workouts (N+1 fetchHevyWorkoutDetail: up to 10 sequential calls in the PT coach, 30 parallel in coach mode), sleep and weight separately. PT_SYSTEM_PROMPT hard-codes 'bro-split: Back/Chest/Leg/Arm/Shoulder days, 3-4x/wk' although athlete_profile holds training_days_per_week. Neither context carries current_program_routines or the engine's next targets or currentAction, so the AI can say 'hold' where the table says 'Ready to increase'.
findings.fix: One `buildTrainingContext()` returning structured data (profile, current program, engine decisions with next targets, muscle dose, recovery, bodyweight from T08). Render it as Turkish text for the PT coach and JSON for coach mode. Drop the hard-coded split. Fetch workouts in one embedded select.

findings.title: Health charts page through raw points client-side with select('*'); the stats rail re-fetches 2× windows under different keys
findings.evidence: fetchHealthMetricSeries loops `.select('*')…range(offset, offset+999)` until a short page. heart_rate arrives about once a minute, so a month is about 43k rows, or about 44 sequential requests including raw jsonb. HealthStatsPanel fetches `win.fetchFrom` (the previous window plus the current one) for the same metric the section already fetched for `from..to`, a different key, so the rows are downloaded twice. SleepSection also fetches a fixed 30-day history alongside its chart range.
findings.fix: Add a Postgres RPC `health_daily_aggregates(metric, from, to, grain)` that applies METRIC_AGGREGATION with the hour-collapse server-side (it would also replace the ai-proxy/phone-gateway copies). At minimum select only the needed columns (date, recorded_at, value->qty, unit, source) and share keys by always fetching the 2× window once.

findings.title: 'Latest'-type mini metrics (VO2 max, cardio recovery, 6-min walk) only look inside the selected window, so they usually show '—'
findings.evidence: `useHealthMetricSeries(metric, window.from, window.to)`, then `if (aggType === 'latest') { const last = series[series.length - 1]; return { value: last?.value ?? null, … } }`. The VO2 max card's own description says it only updates on outdoor walk/run days, so Day and Week views are almost always empty. This is the metric the owner explicitly wants to understand.
findings.fix: For 'latest' metrics fetch a lookback (for example 180 days ending at window.to) and show 'from <date>'. Promote VO2 max, resting HR and HRV to a dedicated 'Fitness & recovery' card with trend and reference bands once age and sex exist (T33).

findings.title: Workout cards never show exercise count or muscle chips (the list query has no exercises)
findings.evidence: getMuscleGroups reads `workout.exercises` and `ex.template?.primary_muscle_group`; `const exerciseCount = workout.exercises?.length ?? null`. fetchHevyWorkouts selects `.from('hevy_workouts').select('*')` only, so exercises is always undefined and both UI branches are dead.
findings.fix: Use an embedded select, `hevy_workouts?select=*,hevy_workout_exercises(exercise_template_id,hevy_exercise_templates(primary_muscle_group))`, or at least `hevy_workout_exercises(count)`. Otherwise delete the dead branches.

findings.title: Workout detail shows every set as 'weight × reps'; duration/distance/assisted exercises read '— × —'
findings.evidence: `{set.weight_kg !== null ? `${set.weight_kg} kg` : '—'}{' × '}{set.reps !== null ? set.reps : '—'}` with a hard-coded 'Weight × reps' column, while decisionParts already has a metric-aware `formatSetLine(set, metricKind)` covering duration, distance and assisted weight.
findings.fix: Move formatSetLine to a shared training/format module, resolve metricKind from the template type (join the template in fetchHevyWorkoutDetail), and use it in the detail, the coach summarizers and the routine chips.

findings.title: Current-program suggestion uses routine last-EDITED time but is labelled 'Recently trained'
findings.evidence: `routines.filter(r => new Date(r.hevy_updated_at).getTime() >= cutoff)`: hevy_updated_at is when the routine was last edited in Hevy. GatingCard says 'Recently trained — looks like your current program?'. A routine trained weekly but not edited in 28 days is not suggested; an abandoned routine edited once is. RECENT_DAYS is duplicated in both files.
findings.fix: Suggest routines by `routine_id` of workouts in the last 28 days (useTrainingHistory already carries routine_id per set). Put the rule in one exported helper.

findings.title: Write-only and read-only settings: muscle preferences have no consumer, target overrides have no editor, training_age_years is unused
findings.evidence: grep: useMusclePreferences is used only by MusclePreferencesList. ProgressTab.tsx:60-68 records that its consumer, MuscleDoseSummary, was removed. useUpsertExerciseTargetOverride and useDeleteExerciseTargetOverride have zero callers, while useProgressData reads the overrides. training_age_years appears only in the type.
findings.fix: Wire priority/exclude_direct into Muscles and Insights (reframe the warnings), add a rep-target editor in the decision drill-down ('Set my target'), and show or remove training_age_years. Otherwise remove the dead UI so the user isn't editing settings that do nothing.

findings.title: Dead code across the training core
findings.evidence: The only references to computeExerciseDecision, computeActionConfidence, computeRpeEvidence, rpeToRir, computeTrendConfidence and the old resolveExpectation are in scripts/verify-progress-decisions.cjs. The same holds for progressCopy statusLabel/decisionHeadline/confidenceLabel/composeConfidenceSentence; statusVerb has no references at all. fetchWorkoutExerciseTemplateIds and fetchWorkoutsWithTemplateIds have no callers. useHealthMetrics and fetchHealthMetrics (limit 5000 over a 1000-row cap) have no callers. fetchHevyWorkouts' from/to are never passed. The 'training' invalidation group is never used.
findings.fix: Keep computeProgramDecision (move it to progress-engine/program.ts), delete the rest, trim verify-progress-decisions.cjs to the program-level assertions, and drop the unused API functions and hook.

findings.title: filterToCurrentProgram and resolveExpectation exist twice
findings.evidence: useProgressData: 'Ported from the retired progressDecisions.ts verbatim', the same body as progressDecisions.filterToCurrentProgram. CurrentProgramPicker's comment still points to progressDecisions.ts::filterToCurrentProgram. resolveExpectation is implemented in both progressDecisions.ts and progress-engine/policies.ts with different signatures.
findings.fix: Export one filterToCurrentProgram and one resolveExpectation from progress-engine. Delete the copies and fix the stale comment.

findings.title: Workout day and 'today' use UTC in some places and local time in others
findings.evidence: fetchTrainingHistory: `dateByWorkout.set(w.id, (w.start_time ?? w.hevy_created_at).slice(0, 10))` takes the UTC date, and TrainingCalendar.workoutDay does the same. TrainingCard and matchedTask use `formatLocalDate(new Date(w.start_time))`. Six files declare `todayStr(){ return new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) }`, shadowing the local shared dateUtils.todayStr. A workout at 00:30 Oslo lands on the previous day in Progress and the calendar but on the right day in Daily; week boundaries roll over late on Monday nights.
findings.fix: Add one `workoutLocalDate(iso)` helper (formatLocalDate(new Date(iso))), use it in fetchTrainingHistory, the calendar and PR dates, and replace every local todayStr with shared dateUtils.todayStr.

findings.title: AI turns that edit training data don't refresh the Training views
findings.evidence: aiWrite contains qk.athlete.profile, limitations and musclePrefs but no qk.hevy.routines(), qk.training.currentProgram, qk.training.ptAssessments or qk.hevy.all. Coach mode's update_hevy_routine/create_hevy_routine write through hevy-api, yet RoutinesTab and useProgressData (routine targets) keep stale data for 5-10 minutes.
findings.fix: Add qk.hevy.routines(), qk.training.currentProgram, qk.training.exerciseTargets and qk.training.ptAssessments to aiWrite, or invalidate the 'training' group after a coach-mode turn.

findings.title: useHevyWorkouts is called with 5+ different limits, ordered by sync time, and the calendar depends on 'latest 200'
findings.evidence: The limits used are 1, 20 (paged), 30, 50 and 200 (×2), each a distinct qk.hevy.workouts(opts) key and a separate request. Results are ordered `.order('hevy_created_at', …)` and the optional filters also use hevy_created_at. useWeekTrainingStats claims 'the same useHevyWorkouts({ limit: 50 }) key everywhere so the list is fetched once', but the other screens use other limits. Months older than the newest 200 workouts render empty in the calendar.
findings.fix: Two hooks: `useHevyWorkoutsRange(from,to)` (ordered by start_time, keyed by range, used by the calendar, week stats and Daily) and `useRecentHevyWorkouts(n)` with one shared n. Order by start_time.

findings.title: useProgressData's full engine memo runs once per consumer
findings.evidence: GatingCard, ProgressOverview and ExerciseDecisionTable each call useProgressData(). The queries dedupe, but each instance runs its own useMemo: buildCanonicalSessions plus evaluateExerciseProgress for every exercise plus the sleep summary over 182 days.
findings.fix: Call useProgressData once in ProgressTab and pass the result down (or through a small context), or move the derivation into a useQuery `select` over a combined key.

findings.title: Decision table: 'Recent changes' equals 'All exercises'; 'All time' actually means 182 days; 'improving' counts 'keep'
findings.evidence: filterByTab: `case 'all': return withDecision … case 'recent': default: return withDecision`, so the two tabs are identical. DATE_WINDOWS `{ id: 'all', label: 'All time' }` sits on a 182-day fetch. `improving = analyzable.filter(d => d.status === 'increase' || d.status === 'keep')` counts BUILD_AT_CURRENT_LOAD as 'improved', inflating the headline 'X of Y improved'.
findings.fix: Define Recent as 'latest session within 14 days with a non-UNCHANGED transition or an event'. Relabel 'Last 6 months'. Count improving as a positive recent trend or a PR/target event. Fewer filters, and lead with a 'Next session' view (T34).

findings.title: Oversized components and modules that should split
findings.evidence: wc -l: WorkedMuscles 807, TrainingCalendar 679, SleepSection 488, BodyMeasurementsTab 361, decisionParts 344, LogHevyWorkoutModal 338, ExerciseDecisionTable 329, HealthStatsPanel 308, RoutineModals 304, HevyTab 274. hevyApi.ts is 702 lines mixing workouts, PRs, progress history, bodyweight (which calls healthApi), routines, templates, sync and edge calls. CLAUDE.md sets a ~150-line component limit.
findings.fix: WorkedMuscles → BodyMap, VerdictBanner, MuscleDetail, BalanceChips plus a pure muscleDose module. TrainingCalendar → WeekView, MonthView, DayDetailPanel files plus a usePlansByDate hook. SleepSection → NightChart, SleepTrendChart, ManualSleepForm. HealthStatsPanel → one file per stats panel. hevyApi → workoutsApi, routinesApi, prsApi, historyApi, syncApi; move bodyweight to the health feature.

findings.title: Four chart implementations; the shared BarLineChart lives inside health/
findings.evidence: Recharts is used directly in 9 files; BarLineChart sits in components/health but is imported by Training's ExerciseProgressChart; BodyMeasurementsTab draws a hand-rolled SVG weight/fat chart (`<path d={weightPath} …>`); decisionParts draws div bars; EnergySection imports TOOLTIP_BOX from training/components/chartKit.
findings.fix: Move BarLineChart, axisFormat, chartKit and the tooltip into shared/ui/charts before the Health split. Replace the hand-rolled SVG and div bars with the shared components (they then get tooltips, a11y and dark mode for free).

findings.title: No age, sex or height stored anywhere, so health numbers can't be put against population norms
findings.evidence: AthleteProfile has goal, experience_level, training_age_years, training_days_per_week, equipment_access and notes only (grep for age/birth/height/sex under training: none). The VO2 max card just says 'higher is fitter'. VO2 max, resting HR, body fat and step norms are age- and sex-specific.
findings.fix: Add birth_year (or date_of_birth), sex and height_cm to athlete_profile (a new migration, pre-migration-safe reads) or a small health_profile table, editable on the new Health page. Build a pure `healthNorms.ts` (VO2 max percentiles by age and sex, resting-HR bands, AASM ≥7 h sleep, step dose-response, BMI/body-fat bands) with a verify script, and cite sources in the UI.

findings.title: The 'plan' is buried: current program lives in the Coach → Profile modal and next-session targets need row expansion
findings.evidence: CurrentProgramPicker is rendered at the bottom of the 'Training profile' ModalShell opened from a ⚙ on the Coach tab. GatingCard tells the user to go to 'Training → Coach → Profile → Current program'. buildNextTargets per-set floors exist in the engine but show only inside DecisionDetail after tapping each row. The owner asks to 'see my plan … what to do'.
findings.fix: Add a Training 'Plan' landing view: the current program (editable in place), the next planned or projected session from useTrainingPlan (T14), and for that routine each exercise's next target from the engine (load × reps per set, with an evidence pill and the reason). Progress, Muscles and History sit behind it.

findings.title: 'Plan routine' payload duplicated; the calendar has no plan action
findings.evidence: Both build `entityModal.open({ kind: 'time-block', config: { heading: 'Plan routine' }, defaults: { title: r.title, category: 'training', color: 'accent', alsoCreateTask: true }, source: { sourceType: 'training_session', sourceId: r.id, taskSourceType: 'training_session' } })`, with only `date` differing. TrainingCalendar day cells can edit plans but not create one.
findings.fix: Add `openPlanRoutine(modal, routine, date?)` in training and use it in RoutinesTab, TrainingCard and a new calendar '+ Plan' action.

findings.title: Sleep is merged by three separate implementations; manual sleep is the only browser writer into health_metrics
findings.evidence: upsertManualSleepEntry upserts three synthetic stage rows (`source: 'manual'`, recorded_at = date 08:00 + i s). computeSleepSummary (client), computeSleepNights (ai-proxy) and computeSleepNightsGw (phone-gateway) each merge nights themselves, so a manual night may be counted differently by the AI or the phone brief than on screen.
findings.fix: Document one sleep contract. Extend verify-ai-sleep-merge.cjs to cover manual rows in all three copies, or move the merge into the RPC from T18 so every surface uses the same SQL.

findings.title: HealthTab runs its own anchor/period state and a second useAnchorDate even when controlled; stale SourceToggle comment
findings.evidence: `const [localAnchor, setLocalAnchor] = useAnchorDate(); const [localPeriod, setLocalPeriod] = useState<Period>('week')` always runs, so two intervals and listeners exist alongside TrainingPage's. The comment 'SourceToggle deliberately stays per-section … (Auto/Apple/Google)' refers to a component deleted with the Fitbit removal.
findings.fix: When moving to /health, let HealthPage own section, anchor and period once (optionally in the URL: ?section=&date=&period=) and pass them down. Drop the uncontrolled fallback and the stale comment.

findings.title: Apple Watch strength workouts (HR/kcal) are never linked to the matching Hevy workout
findings.evidence: health_workouts (HR curve, kcal, raw) is listed only under Health → Overview and opened by a local-state modal, while the Hevy detail shows no HR or energy. The same session exists twice with no connection.
findings.fix: Match by time overlap (health start/end within ±15 min of the Hevy start/end). Show avg/max HR, kcal and the HR curve in the Hevy workout detail, and link back from Health.

findings.title: Daily HealthCard says 'steps today' for any viewed date and links to /training
findings.evidence: `<Sub>steps today</Sub>` renders for whatever `date` prop Daily passes (TodaySummary is shown for every viewed day). `<CellLink to="/training">Details</CellLink>` must become /health after the split.
findings.fix: Label it 'steps' (or 'steps that day'), link to `/health?date=${date}`, and read the data through health-feature hooks.

findings.title: Strava tab totals only the 50 fetched rows, unlabeled
findings.evidence: `useStravaActivities({ limit: 50, … })`, then `<StatTile label="Activities" value={activities.length} />` and a distance/duration total over those rows. It reads like a lifetime total but maxes out at 50.
findings.fix: Use a date window (for example the last 30 days) and label it, or show 'last 50 activities'.

findings.title: Activity ring goals are hard-coded (500 kcal / 30 min / 12 h)
findings.evidence: `const RINGS = [{ key: 'active_energy', …, goal: 500 }, { key: 'apple_exercise_time', goal: 30 }, { key: 'apple_stand_hour', goal: 12 }]`: the header admits 'no per-user goal setting exists yet'.
findings.fix: Store move/exercise/stand goals in the new health profile (or day_targets) and read them here.

findings.title: Health 'week' is a rolling 7 days labelled '(this week)', while Training weeks start Monday
findings.evidence: `if (period === 'week') return { from: shiftStr(anchor, -6), to: anchor }` together with the suffix `' (this week)'`. Training (Progress, insights, Workouts, Home) uses Monday-based weeks, so 'this week' means two different things across tabs.
findings.fix: Relabel it 'last 7 days', or switch Health to calendar weeks. Pick one on the new Health page and state it.

findings.title: isMissingTable is copy-pasted per API file; a sync mutation sits in the wrong hook file
findings.evidence: The same `function isMissingTable(e){ … x?.code === '42P01' || x?.code === 'PGRST205' || /Could not find the table/ … }` appears three times in training alone (plus wishes, water and others). useInitialHevySync is defined in useHevyPRs.ts.
findings.fix: Put `isMissingTable` and `isMissingColumn` in shared/utils/supabaseErrors.ts. Move useInitialHevySync to useHevySync.ts next to the other sync hooks.
